question: With the delayed release of precise guidance documents for Horizon Europe (especially the Annotated Grant Agreement, the publication of which was delayed by two years), beneficiaries have been left in the dark for almost half of the framework programme about what conditions they were agreeing to when signing their required grant agreement. 1.
What negative impacts could the delayed publication of the Annotated Grant Agreement in 2024 have on beneficiaries?
How is the Commission planning to mitigate these negative impacts?
What simplifications and changes to the Commission working method are planned in order to avoid similar delays at the start of the next framework programme?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (17.12.2024) For the current Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF) the Commission launched a comprehensive simplification and harmonisation exercise with the progressive introduction of a common model grant agreement (MGA), set of guidance, including the Annotated Grant Agreement (AGA), and eGrants-use across most directly managed funding programmes.

Applicants and beneficiaries are now benefiting from a harmonised experience, lowering access barriers for participation across programmes. The Commission had to ensure that the guidance, which for most EU programmes never existed in scope and level of support before, fully accommodates the business needs and onboarding of programmes to the MGA and eGrants system.

To allow time for integration, the AGA (and other guidance) were progressively published and updated since 20211, meaning that a wealth of key information was already available prior to the formal publication of the full version 1.0 in May 2024. A harmonised, consolidated and simplified design of the programmes will be key to accelerate implementation and support for beneficiaries under the next MFF.
